highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.159.0 adds experimental image comparison tools and corrects runtime-effect uniform initialization.
highlights_body: The upcoming release also improves Ganesh texture-edge sampling and changes Tizen's CPU blur selection. Linux x86 native assets are no longer packaged.

breaking.title: Move away from Linux x86 native assets
breaking.body: Linux x86 native builds and NuGet package entries have been removed. Applications relying on those assets must move to a supported Linux architecture before upgrading.

bullets.detail: SkiaSharp.Testing adds SKImageComparison for images, bitmaps and pixmaps, with channel tolerances, masks, mismatch budgets, error metrics and difference images. The separately packaged assembly is experimental; opt in by suppressing diagnostic SKIA4001 with NoWarn or a pragma.
New SKRuntimeEffectUniforms buffers start zeroed. Reset() clears the existing buffer in place rather than allocating a replacement, including when uniforms are reused for meshes.
Linear filtering clamps inward to avoid sampling undefined texels outside texture subsets. This affects Ganesh, not CPU or Graphite rendering; texture-edge pixels may differ.

Tizen now applies its blur configuration to Skia itself, selecting the existing ThreeBoxApprox/Tent paths instead of the shader-based Gaussian candidate. Blur pixels and performance may differ; Tizen rendering and performance were not measured in the reported validation.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Restored the Uno Gallery and its view projects to the Windows sample solution.
contributor_summaries.taublast: Fixed uninitialized runtime-effect uniforms and made Reset() clear the existing buffer without replacement allocations.
